Public assets and programs can be structured to attract private capital and earn recurring income.

HAYKALAH works with ministries, authorities, programs and government-owned companies on asset programs, PPP consortia, development companies and Sukuk frameworks. The archive census counts 33 government and sovereign engagements, and the Holy Sites record includes a signed financing process for over SAR 1bn. The current government programs are at framework or proposal stage.

Archive census counts are indicative. The financing outcome is recorded in HAYKALAH files.

What we do

  • Asset-monetization programs for government estates, venues and facilities.

  • PPP consortium architecture, with a permanent DevCo and a ProjectCo for each tender under the PSP Law.

  • Development-company establishment: capital sizing, business plan and formation.

  • Sukuk frameworks that combine Musataha, Istisna’a and Ijara, with one issuer per asset.

  • Pricing models for public services, such as pricing per square meter per pilgrim at the Holy Sites.

  • Bank processes for government-owned developers.

  • Dashboards that report program KPIs to boards and decision makers.

How we work

  1. 01

    Diagnose the program

    Audit the assets, what they cost to hold and the policy goal they serve.

  2. 02

    Design the options

    Each option sets out the structure, the allocation of risk between public and private parties, and the funding route.

  3. 03

    Bring in partners

    Consortium members, operators and banks are selected against clear gates.

  4. 04

    Implement with licensed partners

    Regulated steps run through appropriately licensed institutions, and Shariah structures go to a Shariah board.

  5. 05

    Monitor

    KPIs and variance reporting follow the program after launch.

Questions

What is the PSP Law?

The Private Sector Participation Law, issued by Royal Decree M/63 in 1442H, sets the rules for public-private partnerships and privatization in the Kingdom.

What is a DevCo and ProjectCo structure?

A consortium keeps one permanent development company that holds origination, studies and know-how, and forms a separate project company for each tender. The lead member of each project company can change to suit the tender.

How can a stadium be financed through Sukuk?

In the framework HAYKALAH proposed in 2026, the issuer takes Musataha rights over the land, funds construction through Istisna’a, then leases the completed stadium under an Ijara whose rent pays the Sukuk holders. The framework is a proposal with no mandate.

Are the programs on this site signed mandates?

Not unless stated. The government programs shown on this site are at framework or proposal stage.

Will HAYKALAH name our entity on its website?

No, not without written agreement. Government bodies and clients are described in general terms.

Start with a confidential briefing on the program. An NDA can come first.
